waveName: Wave 3 – Mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform, face guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations, portability

package.title: Readable tables, correct labels, honest truncation, bookmarks and print-at-100 %
package.goal: No text overlaps in tables or key/value blocks. Join labels and column numbers stay off the stones. Coordinate lists say when they are cut off. Fit-to-page uses one standard scale. The PDF has bookmarks, a page column, links and PrintScaling=None. Shared materials are costed correctly. A corrupted palette mapping can never be printed.
steps:
pdfTable.ts: a pure layoutTable(columns:{min, wrap?}[], rows, measure, avail) plus a drawTable wrapper.
- Columns that must not wrap (codes, HEX, numbers, sizes) are sized to their widest cell.
- Text columns share the rest and wrap at spaces or hyphens only.
- Widths only shrink, never stretch; then the font steps down to 7 and 6.5 pt.
- Never ellipsize or split an identifier.
- Multi-line rows have their own height; the page-break test uses that height.
- Wrapped header band.
- Replace table() in pdf.ts with it.

Key/value blocks on the cover, section cover and material summary: label width = max measured label + 3 mm, wrapped. The section cover moves the mini-map below the block when the page is narrower than 140 mm. The legend gets separate Material and Farbnr. columns.

Page numbers at baseline PH-6.5. Laying-sheet footers read 'Blatt A1-1 · Seite 9 / 74'. Add a rotText helper that never passes align or baseline together with angle. Use it for the right-edge join label (inside the margin, vertically centred, moved to sideInfo if too long) and for rotated column numbers.

Coordinate list: set truncated exactly where a piece is skipped, using a labelled outer loop. The per-section title reads 'erste N von M Steinen – Rest siehe CSV' or 'vollständig'. Print the notice directly under the last table. Use one cellPieces-based count.

pdfOptions.ts: add fitSheetScale(allSections, printW, printH). It takes the minimum over ALL sections and snaps DOWN to a standard series (4, 3, 2, 1, 1/1.25, 1/1.5, 1/2, 1/2.5, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, …, 1/100). Add sheetPrintArea(PW, PH) and fmtScale ('1:1,5'). Use them everywhere, including the cover.

doc.setProperties({title: 'MosaicPlan – <name>'}) and viewerPreferences({PrintScaling:'None', DisplayDocTitle:true}). Record page numbers while generating and build an outline: chapters, then sections, then sheets. Use raw Unicode titles, not safe(). Add a 'Seite' column to the overview section table, filled in afterwards, with doc.link rows and links on the overview map. Add links on the section mini-map boxes.
Material list: use stats.perMaterial (packs, toBuy, cost per material, 'ohne Material' group, missing-material marks). Use paletteDisplayName for colour names.
Guard: if stats.invalidColorPieces > 0 or maxColorIndex ≥ palette.length (src/core/integrity.ts), throw a translated error instead of drawing.
acceptance: Unit test of layoutTable boxes: no two boxes intersect and all lie within [M, PW-M], for de and tr with 40-character material names and 'VT-1000-GLOSS' colour numbers, on A4 and on 120×297 mm. Each colour number stays one token.
Coordinate notice: present for a single section with coordLimit = pieces-1; present for a multi-section project with the limit inside the last section; absent when coordLimit ≥ pieces.
Output contains /Outlines, /PrintScaling /None and /Title. Each section's outline entry points to a page whose header contains 'Abschnitt <id>'.
Fit mode: 600×800 mm on A4 shows a single scale string on all sheets; 500×700 mm on A3 landscape snaps to 1:1.
The existing PDF==preview per-colour fill test still passes. A tampered palette index makes generatePdf reject.
package.risk: Effort L. Many small layout changes in one file; run the pdftotext overlap check from the audit before merging. The page count may change slightly.

findings.title: Table cells wrap into the next row and headers overlap (legend, material list, coordinates, section cover)
findings.problem: table() wraps cell text with maxWidth but keeps a fixed row height of 5 mm (pdf.ts:175-188), so any wrapped cell prints over the next row. Headers are not wrapped at all. Column widths are fixed mm arrays that ignore page width. The section-cover key/value block uses a fixed 45 mm label column (pdf.ts:485-491), but the 'Fuge zum Nachbarabschnitt' label is wider than that.
findings.evidence: overlap.py (pdftotext -bbox word-box intersection): out/materials.pdf has 95 overlapping word pairs on the legend and material pages alone (p3=41, p4=54) with realistic names such as 'Sicis Vetrite Collezione Grande Iridium' (png/mat-03.png, png/mat-04.png). Coordinate rows: 'Individuell zugeschnitten' prints over the next row's 'Quadrat' (png/a3c-40-crop.png). Every legend: '+10 % Reserve' x 'Material'. Every section cover: 'Nachbarabschnitt' x '1 mm' (png/a5-08.png). Section legend header reads 'zugeschnittenRohsteine'. Totals per PDF: a4p_5mm 123, a3l 146, many_templates 115, tr_a4 122 overlapping word pairs.
findings.proposal: In table(): for each row, compute lines = doc.splitTextToSize(cell, w-1.5) per cell. Set rowH = max(1, maxLines)*3.2 + 1.8 and draw multi-line text explicitly. Use that height for the page-break test. Allow 2-line headers (split header strings the same way; header band height = max lines). Scale the width arrays to the page: widths = widths.map(w => w*(PW-2M)/sum(widths)), so A3 and custom paper use their width. For the section-cover and cover key/value blocks, set labelW = max(getTextWidth(label)) + 3. In the legend and material list, split 'manufacturer product' and 'colour number' into separate columns, and shorten with an ellipsis instead of wrapping when a cell exceeds 2 lines.
corrected:
In src/core/pdf.ts, rewrite the table() helper (lines 141-190). For a high-volume table (coordinates), consider jspdf-autotable, but a hand-written fix is enough:

1. Line height. lineH = doc.getFontSize() * doc.getLineHeightFactor() / doc.internal.scaleFactor (about 3.25 mm at 8 pt).

2. Data rows. For each row, split every string cell with doc.splitTextToSize(safe(c), widths[i] - 1.5). Set thisRowH = rowH + (maxLines - 1) * lineH. This keeps the caller's rowH (5 or 4.2) as the height of a single-line row, so coordinate pages do not grow.
   - Before drawing, test y + thisRowH - 3.6 > PH - M - 8 for the page break.
   - Draw with doc.text(lines, x, y).
   - Draw the separator at y + thisRowH - 3.6.
   - Then y += thisRowH.

3. Header. Split header labels the same way, using the bold font. The header band height is rowH + (maxHeaderLines - 1) * lineH, and the band rect uses that height.

4. Widths.
   - avail = PW - 2*M. If sum(widths) > avail, scale every width by avail/sum. When that factor is below about 0.85, also lower the table font, but never below 6 pt.
   - Scale up only tables designed to be full width (sum >= 0.9*190: overview, legend, material list, section legend, coordinates). Leave the 2-column per-shape and per-size tables as they are.
   - This fixes custom paper: at 120 mm, the overview and legend columns currently fall off the page.

5. Never shorten text in these tables. Wrap it instead. In particular, no ellipsis for colour numbers, codes, counts or sizes. Optionally, in the legend only, show manufacturer and colour number on two lines (manufacturer\ncolourNumber) instead of one long string.

6. Key/value blocks: cover (line 242, M+55), material summary (line 367, M+70) and section cover (line 490, M+45).
   - Compute labelW = min(max(getTextWidth(label in bold 9 pt)) + 3, 0.45*avail).
   - Also wrap labels with splitTextToSize(label, labelW - 2).
   - Advance y by the larger of the label line count and the value line count.

7. Regression check, under e2e or a node script, not vitest. Generate PDFs in de and tr with long material names, on A4 and on a 120 mm custom page. Run pdftotext -bbox and assert zero intersecting word boxes on pages whose header is legend, materials, section cover or coordinates. Exclude the laying sheets: their joining-mark label overlaps are a separate issue.

Rewrite table() in src/core/pdf.ts (lines 140-189) to use measured column specs, and fix the three key/value blocks. Only layout changes; no number, count or dimension changes.

1) Column specs: replace widths:number[] with {min:number, wrap?:boolean}[].
- Columns that must never wrap: code, swatch, HEX, CIELAB, colour number, X/Y, sizes, counts, packs, price, cut flag.
  - Width = max(spec.min, widest cell or widest header word measured with getTextWidth at the current font + 2 mm).
- Text columns that may wrap: name, material/product, shape.
  - They share the remaining width (avail = PW-2M), each capped at about 80 mm.
- Scale factor = min(1, avail/sum). Never stretch a table to fill A3/A2 width; leave the space empty.
- If the non-wrapping columns alone exceed avail (custom paper of 100-150 mm), shrink in this order:
  - lower the table font to 7 pt, then 6.5 pt;
  - then move CIELAB into a second line under the name.
  - Never split an identifier by characters.
- Wrap text columns only at spaces/hyphens. Use doc.splitTextToSize(safe(c), w-1.5) only for wrap columns.

2) Row layout:
- n = maximum lines in the row; extra = (n-1)*3.25 mm (8 pt × 1.15 line factor).
- Page-break test: if (y + extra > PH - M - 8).
- Draw multi-line cells with doc.text(lines, x, y). Keep the swatch top-aligned.
- Separator line at y + extra + 1.4; then y += rowH + extra.
- Header: wrap at word boundaries only, band height = rowH + (maxHeaderLines-1)*3.25, redraw after each page break.

3) Never truncate or ellipsize any cell. Colour numbers, product names, codes and quantities must print in full (requirement 18; this is the shopping list).

4) Key/value blocks:
- Measure labelW = max(getTextWidth(safe(label)) in bold 9 pt) + 3 mm for:
  - the cover (pdf.ts:229-237, currently fixed 55);
  - the section cover (pdf.ts:485-491, currently fixed 45);
  - the material summary (pdf.ts:368-374, currently fixed M+70, value not wrapped).
- Value width = max(40, PW-2M-labelW-reserve), wrapped with splitTextToSize.
- Section cover: if PW-2M-labelW < 140 mm, draw the mini sheet overview below the key/value block instead of at the right (reserve 0 instead of 75). This removes the negative width that prints one character per line on custom paper narrower than about 140 mm.

5) Legend (pdf.ts:333): replace 'manufacturer colorNumber' with two columns: Material = manufacturer + product (wrap) and Farbnr. (no wrap). The material list already has the split.

6) Regression test (tests/pdf-layout.test.ts):
- Wrap the jsPDF instance (or factor out a pure layoutTable() that returns cell boxes).
- Cases: de/en/tr × {A4 portrait, A3 landscape, custom 120×297}, with 40-character material names and colour numbers like 'VT-1000-GLOSS'.
- Assert:
  - no two text boxes on a page intersect;
  - every box lies within [M, PW-M] × [M, PH-M];
  - every colour number appears as one unbroken token;
  - the joint value string appears unobstructed on each section cover.

Out of scope here: the overlaps on laying-sheet pages (joining labels over cell codes) are a separate issue.

findings.title: Page number and header sit inside typical printers' non-printable margin
findings.problem: Page numbers are drawn at PH-3.5 mm (pdf.ts:874) and the running header at M-3 = 7 mm baseline (pdf.ts:127). Many laser and inkjet printers cannot print within about 4–5 mm of the edge. On a 500–1100-page plan, clipped page numbers make it hard to sort the pages.
findings.evidence: pdftotext -bbox on out/a4p_5mm_1to1.pdf p9: 'Seite 9 / 74' has its bottom 2.9 mm from the bottom page edge; the header 'MosaicPlan' starts 4.4 mm from the top edge.
findings.proposal: Move the page number to ≥ 7 mm from the edge (e.g. y = PH - M + 3 on the footer line, which needs the footer reduction from the paper-waste finding) and the header to ≥ 6 mm. On laying sheets, repeat the sheet ID next to the page number ('A1-1 · Seite 9/74'), so pages stay identifiable when margins are trimmed for joining.
corrected:
In src/core/pdf.ts:874, change the page-number baseline from PH - 3.5 to PH - 6.5 (or PH - 7). The ink then sits about 6.3-8.3 mm above the bottom edge, clear of 4-5 mm printer margins. The band from 0 to 12 mm above the bottom edge is otherwise empty on every page type, so no other layout change is needed.

Optionally, to give the header a safety margin as well, set header font(7), baseline M - 2 = 8 mm, and move the rule to M - 1 (pdf.ts:125-131). Header ink then starts at about 6.2 mm, and the rule still sits above the first content at M + 3.5.

Optionally, append the sheet ID to the footer on laying sheets ('A1-1 · Seite 9 / 74'). To do that, record a page→sheetId map in drawSheet (pdf.ts:550) and read it in the page-number loop. This is only a convenience: the sheet ID is already printed at 13.5 mm on each laying sheet. Do not claim it survives trimming to the grid edge, because nothing outside the grid does.

Add one assertion to tests/pdf.test.ts: with jsPDF, or with pdftotext -bbox on a generated A4 PDF, check that the 'Seite' text's yMax is at least 6 mm above the bottom edge.

In src/core/pdf.ts:
(1) Add a constant `const SAFE = 6; // mm, printer-safe inset (laser ≈4.2 mm, many inkjets 5 mm bottom)`.
(2) In the page-number loop (line 874), draw at baseline `PH - SAFE - 0.5` (ink about 6.5-8.3 mm from the bottom). This lies inside the existing empty 10 mm bottom margin. The nearest other content on every page type is at ≥13 mm, so no other layout change is needed and it does not depend on the paper-waste/footer-reduction finding.
(3) Make the footer label page-type aware. Keep the existing footer loop and store a per-page label: have newPage() take an optional `footerId` (and drawSheet pass `${sec.id}-${ti}`), or push `{page: doc.getNumberOfPages(), id}` into an array. Laying sheets then print `Blatt A1-1 · Seite 9 / 74`, using the existing i18n keys pdf.sheet and pdf.page; add no new strings. All other pages keep `Seite 9 / 74`. This keeps sheets identifiable after the top/left overlap trim, which removes the header and the title at pdf.ts:551.
(4) Optional: move the running header baseline from M-3 to M-2.2 and the rule from M-1.5 to M-0.9. This raises the header ink start from 4.8 mm to about 5.6 mm. It is still clear of the sheet title (cap top ≈11 mm) and the table starts (≥ M+7).
(5) Regression test (vitest): wrap or spy on jsPDF `text` in a small generatePdf run (A4 and custom 150×150) and assert that every text call's y is ≥ SAFE + cap height from the top and ≤ PH - SAFE from the bottom, and that x is within [SAFE, PW - SAFE]. This keeps future footer or legend changes from creeping back into the unprintable band.
Do not move or rescale the laying grid, joining marks or the 50/100 mm control line; this is a text-only change.

findings.title: The 'join to next sheet' label on the right edge prints over the stones of the last column
findings.problem: The right join label is drawn with doc.text(..., { angle: -90, align: 'center' }) (pdf.ts:674). jsPDF applies the centre alignment as a horizontal shift before rotating, so the rotated text moves about half its length to the left, into the mosaic. It covers the colour codes of the last column on every sheet that has a right-hand neighbour.
findings.evidence: png/a5hi-09-right.png (300 dpi crop of out/a4p_5mm_1to1.pdf p9): 'Anschluss Blatt A1-2 →' runs vertically across the stones of column 29 (codes 23/21/04). The same happens in png/a12-09.png (12 mm, column 14) and png/fit-09.png (column 28). overlap.py also flags p12 '16' x '→'.
findings.proposal: Do not use align for rotated text. Compute w = doc.getTextWidth(label) and call doc.text(label, px(rightE) + 1.5, py((topE+botE)/2) - w/2, { angle: -90 }); with -90° the glyphs extend to the right, into the 10 mm margin. Alternatively print it horizontally in the bottom-right footer next to the existing '← / ↑' side info (pdf.ts:687-688). Add a check that no text box intersects the mosaic rectangle px(X0)..px(X1).
corrected:
In src/core/pdf.ts, add a small helper for rotated text that never passes `align` or `baseline` to jsPDF when an angle is set. Compute the anchor from the text width instead:

```ts
const rotText = (s: string, cx: number, cy: number, angle: 90 | -90, gap: number) => {
  const str = safe(s);
  const w = doc.getTextWidth(str);
  if (angle === -90) doc.text(str, cx + gap, cy - w / 2, { angle: -90 });      // runs down, glyphs extend to the right
  else doc.text(str, cx + gap, cy + w / 2, { angle: 90 });                       // runs up, glyphs extend to the left
};
```

1. Right join label (pdf.ts:674). Measure first: `const lbl = safe(`${t('pdf.joinTo')} ${lr} →`); const w = doc.getTextWidth(lbl); const hSheet = py(botE) - py(topE);`.
   - If `w <= hSheet - 8`, so the label stays clear of the corner crosses at ±3 mm, call `doc.text(lbl, px(rightE) + 1.5, py((topE + botE) / 2) - w / 2, { angle: -90 })`. The text then sits in the right page margin, vertically centred on the sheet.
   - Otherwise, for short sheets, leave it out there and add `→ ${lr}` to the existing footer `sideInfo` list (pdf.ts:687-688, next to ← and ↑). The footer also gains a consistent → entry on every sheet that has one.
2. Rotated column numbers (pdf.ts:612, used when cs===1 and pitch < 5 mm), same root cause. Replace the rotated branch with `doc.text(lbl, xc + capH * 0.35, T - 9 + w / 2, { angle: 90 })`, where `xc = px(colX + colW/2)`, `w = doc.getTextWidth(lbl)` and `capH = fontSize * 0.3528`. This centres each number on its own column. Today the numbers are offset about 1.3–1.9 mm, onto the joint to the left neighbour. Keep the unrotated branch as it is.
3. Regression test (vitest). `vi.spyOn(jsPDF.API, 'text')` while generating a small 2-sheet PDF, for example 3 mm tiles at 1:1 on A4.
   - Assert that no recorded call combines a numeric angle with `align` or `baseline`.
   - For every call whose string starts with t('pdf.joinTo'), assert x >= px(rightE). Alternatively, in e2e, check with `pdftotext -bbox` that the join label's xMin is at least the mosaic's right edge.

Do not change any geometry, cross, ruler, count or grid code.

findings.title: Coordinate list is cut off silently, with no notice (violates requirement 18)
findings.problem: In the coordinate loop (pdf.ts:824-846) the row/col loops stop on `written < opts.coordLimit` without setting `truncated`. The flag is only set when the limit is hit in the middle of a multi-piece cell (pdf.ts:828-830) or when another selected section follows (pdf.ts:818-820). For a single-section project, or when the limit is reached at a cell boundary in the last section, the PDF ends without the 'gekürzt' notice. The list looks complete but is not.
findings.evidence: Repro /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/pdf-print/trunc.ts prints "cells=256 coordLimit=100 coordRowsPrinted=100 truncationNoticePresent=false" (and the same for 200). In out/a4p_5mm_1to1.pdf (coordLimit 3000, 3655 stones) the list ends at BC029 on the last page (png/a5-74.png) although section B1 runs to row BO / col 51. `grep -c gekürzt` on the extracted text returns 0.
findings.proposal: Before the loop, count the pieces of the selected sections (sum of computeStats(...range).pieces, or sectionPieceCount). After the loop set truncated = written < totalSelectedPieces. Print the notice on the last coordinate page itself, directly under the table, not only on a separate page. Put a status in each section's table title, e.g. 'Koordinaten A1 (1.734 von 1.852 Steinen – Rest siehe CSV)'. Add a vitest case: single section with coordLimit < pieces must contain the notice.
corrected:
In src/core/pdf.ts (coordinate block, about lines 814-864), decide truncation from the loop itself instead of comparing against a separately computed total:
1. Remove `&& written < opts.coordLimit` from the row and column loop conditions. Use a labelled outer loop (`outer: for (let row ...)`).
2. Inside the column loop, call `const ps = cellPieces(...)`. Then: `if (ps.length && written >= opts.coordLimit) { truncated = true; secTruncated = true; break outer; }`. Keep the existing forEach guard for a cell cut in the middle. That guard should also set secTruncated.
3. Keep the existing check between sections (818-820).
4. If secTruncated, add the status to the section's table title, for example `Koordinaten – Abschnitt A1 (erste 1.734 Steine – gekürzt, vollständige Liste als CSV)`. Count the number shown with the same cellPieces-based count the loop uses. Also print the existing pdf.coordsTruncated text right under the last table. Keep the separate notice page as well, or replace it with this.
5. Add a vitest case in tests/pdf.test.ts: a single section with squares only and coordLimit smaller than the pieces must contain the notice. A second case selects only the last section via sectionIds with a small coordLimit. A third case with coordLimit at or above the pieces must not contain the notice.
Optionally, align sectionPieceCount with cellPieces (LINE without line data = 1 piece), so the overview's per-section stone counts match the lists.

findings.title: 'Fit to page' uses a different scale per section but still tells the user to overlay sheets
findings.problem: With sheetScale=0, each section gets s = min(printW/sec.w, printH/sec.h) (pdf.ts:457). Sections of different size therefore print at different scales, and the scale shown is an odd value like '0,709:1'. The sheets still draw registration crosses and the hint 'Blätter an den Passkreuzen deckungsgleich auflegen', which cannot work across sections.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/pdf-print/measure_fit_a4.txt (content-stream measurement of out/fit_a4.pdf): sections A1–A3 at 0.709:1 (8 mm stone printed as 5.673 mm), A4 at 0.73:1 (5.836 mm). Over a 242 mm section height, neighbouring sheets differ by about 5 mm. pdftotext p9 still contains the 'deckungsgleich auflegen' hint.
findings.proposal: In fit mode, compute one scale for all selected sections: s = min over sections, then round down to a standard reduction (1:1.25, 1:1.5, 1:2, 1:2.5, 1:3, 1:4, 1:5, …). Print it the conventional way ('Maßstab 1:1,5'). If the scales still differ (e.g. a single section was exported), drop the crosses and the markHint and print 'nicht maßstäblich – nur Orientierung'. Mirror the chosen scale in the StepPdf estimate.
corrected:
1. In src/core/pdfOptions.ts, add one shared helper so the PDF and the UI agree:
   `export function fitSheetScale(sections: {w:number;h:number}[], printW: number, printH: number): number`
   - Compute `raw` with a plain loop (not Math.min(...spread), so thousands of sections are safe): the minimum over ALL sections of `min(printW/w, printH/h)`.
   - Snap down to the largest standard value that is ≤ raw + 1e-9 from [4, 3, 2, 1, 1/1.25, 1/1.5, 1/2, 1/2.5, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, 1/10, 1/20, 1/50, 1/100]. If none qualifies, fall back to raw.
   - Also export `sheetPrintArea(PW, PH)`, returning {printW: PW-32, printH: PH-50}, and use it in both places. This fixes the PH-53 vs PH-50 mismatch.

2. In src/core/pdf.ts, before the section loop (around line 455):
   - Compute `const fitScale = fitSheetScale(input.sections.sections, printW, printH)`. Use all sections, not `selected`, so separate exports of single sections print at the same scale.
   - Use `const s = opts.sheetScale > 0 ? opts.sheetScale : fitScale`.
   - Add a formatter: `fmtScale(s) = s >= 1 ? \`${f1(s)}:1\` : \`1:${f1(1/s)}\``. Use it at lines 483 and 554. On the cover (line 232), show `${t('pdf.fitPage')} (${fmtScale(fitScale)})`.
   - The crosses and markHint can stay: with one global scale, neighbouring sheets now line up at the crosses.
   - The tilesOf split stays at one sheet per section, because s ≤ printW/sec.w and s ≤ printH/sec.h for every section.

3. In src/ui/project/StepPdf.tsx:
   - Compute the same fitScale from G.sections with the shared helpers.
   - Show it on the fit option, e.g. "An Seite anpassen (1:1,5)".
   - Use `opts.sheetScale || fitScale` in tooSmallCodes (line 37) instead of `|| 1`.

4. Add a vitest that generates a fit-mode PDF for a 600x800 mm project (A4 portrait, 300 mm sections). Assert that pdftotext-equivalent text (or the drawn cell widths) shows exactly one scale value across all sheets. Also assert that the 500x700 mm project on A3 landscape snaps to 1:1.

1. Add a pure helper in src/core/pdfOptions.ts that both pdf.ts and StepPdf use, so they cannot drift apart.
   - Signatures: `sheetPrintArea(PW, PH) => {printW: PW-32, printH: PH-50}` and `effectiveSheetScale(opts, allSections, printW, printH)`.
   - Move the reserve constants (M=10, left 12, top 19, bottom 21) there too. StepPdf currently uses PH-53 while pdf.ts uses PH-50.
   - If sheetScale > 0, return it unchanged.
   - Otherwise compute raw = min over **all** project sections (input.sections.sections, not only the selected ones) of min(printW/sec.w, printH/sec.h). Then round raw down to the largest value from a standard series that is <= raw. Series: 4, 3, 2, 1.5, 1, then 1/1.25, 1/1.5, 1/2, 1/2.5, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, 1/6, 1/8, 1/10, 1/15, 1/20, …; below the series use 1/ceil(1/raw).
   - This gives one fixed scale per project and paper format, no matter which sections are exported or when, so the registration crosses and the "deckungsgleich auflegen" hint stay correct.
2. In pdf.ts:
   - Compute `s` once before the section loop (replacing line 457).
   - Print the scale in the usual German way through one formatter used at lines 232, 483 and 554: s >= 1 gives "2:1", s < 1 gives "1:" + f1(1/s, 2) (e.g. "1:1,5"). The cover (232) shows the actual scale plus "(an Seite angepasst)".
   - When s != 1, add a short line to the sheet footer, e.g. 'pdf.notFullSize': "Nicht 1:1 – nicht als Auflegevorlage unter die Steine verwenden; Maße über das mm-Lineal ablesen." The ruler already shows absolute mm values, so nothing new is invented.
3. In StepPdf.tsx:
   - Use effectiveSheetScale for the sheet estimate.
   - In `tooSmallCodes`, replace `(opts.sheetScale || 1)` with the effective scale so the "codes too small" warning also appears in fit mode.
   - Show the resulting scale next to the "An Seite anpassen" button.
4. Add a test in tests/pdf.test.ts:
   - Use a 1000x1200 mm, 8 mm, 300 mm-section layout with sheetScale 0 on A4.
   - Assert that effectiveSheetScale gives one value <= every section's fit value, and that each section's tilesOf produces exactly 1 sheet.
   - Assert that a PDF of only section A1 and a PDF of all sections report the same scale string.

findings.title: Large PDFs have no bookmarks, no page references and no 'print at 100 %' default
findings.problem: Large projects produce PDFs of hundreds or thousands of pages. They have no outline/bookmarks, no table of contents, no page column in the overview's section table (pdf.ts:297-301) and no clickable sections. findings.title: Auto colour names are wrong and duplicated in the legend and PDF (pure red = 'Orange', 8× 'Blassblau')
findings.problem: describeColor() applies HSV-style hue cut-offs to CIELAB hue angles. sRGB red has h_ab of about 40°, so every red is named Orange, Dunkelorange or Dunkelbraun; blue becomes 'Dunkelviolett' and yellow 'Hellgelbgrün'. Names are also not unique: the portrait legend has 8× Blassblau, 7× Dunkelbraun and 4× Hellbeige, and the red sweater is listed as 'Dunkelbraun'. These names go into the legend, the palette table and the PDF that the user shops and lays from.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-desktop/ts/names.out: '#FF0000 h=40.0 -> Orange', '#C00000 -> Orange', '#800000 -> Dunkelorange', '#841929 -> Dunkelbraun', '#0000FF -> Dunkelviolett', '#FFFF00 -> Hellgelbgrün'. Legend: shots/j2-09-colors-after-compute.png (codes 06-20 = Blassblau ×8, 25/27-32 = Dunkelbraun ×7). PDF: `pdftotext portrait.pdf | grep -c Blassblau` = 29. Code: src/core/color.ts describeColor() (the 'if (h < 20 || h >= 345) base = red' chain).
findings.proposal: Replace the hue chain with nearest-reference naming. Keep a curated table of about 40 named reference colours per language (German: Rot, Karminrot, Weinrot, Rosa, Lachs, Terrakotta, Orange, Ocker, Gelb, Oliv, Grün, Türkis, Hellblau, Blau, Marine, Violett, Braun, Beige, Haut hell/mittel/dunkel, Grau …) stored as Lab, and pick the name by minimum ΔE2000. Then make names unique inside a palette: when several entries share a name, append a lightness rank by L* ('Blassblau hell / mittel / dunkel', then '… 1/2/3'). Store PaletteColor.autoName=true so auto names are regenerated on language switch (today Turkish names stay after switching back to DE, see journey3 output), while user-edited names are kept.

- Prototype that confirms the approach: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/verify-ux-desktop-3/proto.ts

2) Make names unique within a palette.
- Add a helper `nameAutoPalette(palette, lang)` in src/core/edits.ts.

4) Tests in tests/core.test.ts:
- `describeColor(hexToLab('#FF0000'), 'de')` is 'Rot'; '#0000FF' gives 'Blau'; '#FFFF00' gives 'Gelb'; '#8B4513' contains 'braun'.

- After changing language, auto names change and a user-edited name stays the same.

Impact 3-4, effort S-M.

1. **Rewrite describeColor().** In src/core/color.ts, keep one table of about 50 reference colours. Each entry has a Lab value and a name in de, en and tr. Do not keep separate tables per language.
   - Include common tile and portrait colours: Rot, Dunkelrot (#8B0000), Karminrot, Weinrot, Bordeaux, Rosa, Altrosa, Pink, Magenta, Lachs, Apricot, Terrakotta, Rostbraun, Orange (#FFA500 and #F08000), Ocker, Senfgelb, Gelb, Hellgelb, Oliv, Gelbgrün, Hellgrün, Grün, Dunkelgrün, Salbeigrün, Türkis, Petrol, Hellblau, Himmelblau, Blau, Taubenblau, Graublau, Stahlblau/dunkles Graublau (#3C5670), Marineblau, Violett, Flieder, Aubergine, Hellbraun, Braun, Dunkelbraun, Beige, Sand, Creme, Haut hell/mittel/dunkel.
   - Keep the existing grey branch first: if chroma C* < ~6, name the colour Weiß/Hellgrau/Grau/Dunkelgrau/Schwarz by L* alone.
   - Otherwise pick the reference with the smallest ΔE2000.
   - If that smallest ΔE is above ~8 and |ΔL*| is above 12, add "Hell"/"Dunkel" in front, using the existing prefix and lowercasing rules.

2. **Pin the names with tests in tests/core.test.ts, for all three languages.**
   - #FF0000→Rot, #800000→Dunkelrot, #841929→Weinrot, #FFA500→Orange, #FFFF00→Gelb, #0000FF→Blau, #008000→Grün, #DFA382→Haut*, #8B4513→Braun.
   - The existing white, black and #9fc5f8 checks.
   - Use the portrait palette hexes from j2-09 as further cases.
   - For a starting point see /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/value-ux-desktop-3/proto.ts and proto.out in the same folder.

3. **Track which names are automatic.** Add an optional `autoName?: boolean` to PaletteColor in src/core/types.ts.
   - Set it to true wherever describeColor supplies the name: mosaic.ts:579 and edits.ts:155.
   - Carry it through the fixed-palette data at mosaic.ts:462 and 468, so a recompute keeps it.
   - Set it to false when the user types a name (StepColors.tsx:193) or adopts a material colour name (StepColors.tsx:122).
   - When the colours are recomputed, the UI language changes, or a PDF is exported, regenerate only names where autoName is true.
   - Saved projects without the flag: mark a name as automatic only if it equals legacyDescribeColor(lab, de|en|tr). Keep the current function under that name just for this check. Otherwise keep the name as it is.

4. **Optionally, make repeated names easier to tell apart.** Do this only for automatic names, and only when the same name appears more than once in a palette.
   - Add a qualifier based on lightness order within that group: (hell/dunkel) for 2, (hell/mittel/dunkel) for 3, and "sehr hell … sehr dunkel" for up to 5.
   - Never add numbers, because they would clash with the two-digit colour code.
   - Beyond 5, let the name repeat; the colour code stays the unique identifier.
   - Keep names to about 22 characters or less so the PDF legend column still fits.

This changes only the labels. Codes, counts, Lab and HEX values, and geometry are untouched, and no code looks anything up by colour name.

findings.title: 'Palette aus Materialien' after a compute swaps the palette without remapping stones, so the whole mosaic changes colours (black face)
findings.problem: In custom-palette mode, the 'Palette aus Materialien' button calls api.setPalette() with a freshly built array in material order. The computed mosaic stores palette indices, and compute had already re-sorted the palette by lightness. Every stone therefore silently gets another colour: the face becomes black and the hair light blue. The preview, the stats and the PDF all use the scrambled mapping. Only the generic stale badge appears. Other paths that change palette length or order without remapping can produce indices ≥ palette.length.
findings.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t12_palette_replace_after_compute.cjs, output t12_output.txt. Before: '02 Haut hell 300 | 03 Hellblau 1.176 | ... | 10 Schwarz 215'. After: '02 Schwarz 300 | 03 Haut hell 1.176 | ... | 10 Grau 215 | 11 Gruen 0 | 12 Rosa 0'. Same stone counts, different colours. Side-by-side t12-before-after.png in the same folder. Code: StepColors.tsx:144-155 (setPalette(p) with no remap, even when api.computed exists); compare removePaletteColor in edits.ts:174-193, which does remap.
findings.proposal: Add a remapPalette(oldPalette, newPalette, data, formula) helper to edits.ts. It maps each old index to its new index by materialId, then exact hex, then nearest ΔE, and rewrites c1/c2/sub/free via remapAll. Call it from every palette-replacing action when api.computed is set ('Palette aus Materialien', and any future import), followed by touchMosaic(). Otherwise disable the button after compute, with the hint 'Erst neu berechnen'. Add an invariant check (max index < palette.length) in the loader and before PDF/CSV generation, and show an error instead of printing wrong colours.
corrected:
The direction is right. Here it is made precise:

(1) In src/core/edits.ts, add `export function remapToPalette(oldP: PaletteColor[], newP: PaletteColor[], data: MosaicData, formula): void`.
- Build a lookup `map[old] -> new` for each old index: same materialId first, then the same hex (case-insensitive), then the nearest new colour by ΔE (NearestColorMatcher over newP.lab).
- Apply it with the existing remapAll. Export remapAll or call it internally.

(2) In StepColors.tsx, change the 'Palette aus Materialien' onClick:
- When api.computed is set, call remapToPalette(palette, p, api.computed.data, rec.settings.deltaE), then api.setPalette(p), then api.touchMosaic(). This is the same order remove() already uses at lines 111-114.
- Keep the stale state, since cp changes, so the user is still asked to recompute. Ask for confirmation first, e.g. 'Mosaik wird auf die neue Palette umgefärbt (nächste Farbe) – für ein optimales Ergebnis neu berechnen'.
- The simpler alternative is to hide or disable this button while api.computed exists and show 'Erst neu berechnen'.

(3) Add an invariant so wrong results can never be printed silently:
- In src/core/stats.ts:172-173, count stones whose index is out of range in an `invalidColorPieces` counter instead of skipping them with `continue`.
- In StepPdf.tsx, StepPlan.tsx and the CSV export, refuse to generate output and show an error ('Farbzuordnung ungültig – bitte neu berechnen') when that counter is above 0, or when a max-index scan of c1/c2/sub/free is ≥ palette.length.
- When useProject.ts loads a mosaic, run the same scan. If it fails, mark the project as needing a recompute instead of rendering magenta stones.

(4) Add a vitest that computes in custom mode, replaces the palette in another order with fewer entries, applies the remap, and then checks two things: every index is below palette.length, and the stats piece total still equals the total from geometry.

1) StepColors.tsx:144-152, the 'Palette aus Materialien' button. When api.computed is null, keep today's replace behaviour. When api.computed exists, MERGE so that existing indices and codes stay stable:
   a) For each material with a valid hex that is not yet in the palette (match by materialId, then by exact upper-case hex), append it with addPaletteColor(..., m.id). Appending never invalidates an index.
   b) Find the palette entries that have no material counterpart, i.e. no materialId among the current materials and no exact hex match. Remove them in DESCENDING index order with the existing removePaletteColor(palette, api.computed.data, i, undefined, rec.settings.deltaE), which already moves their stones to the nearest remaining colour by ΔE. Before applying, count the affected stones from api.stats.perColor and show a confirm dialog such as 'N Steine werden auf die nächste Materialfarbe umgestellt (max. ΔE x) – fortfahren?'. Afterwards show the same numbers as a notice.
   c) Call api.setPalette(next) and then api.touchMosaic(). Leave the stale badge on, because a recompute could make use of the newly added colours.
   If you want a single helper, put mergePaletteFromMaterials(palette, data, materials, formula) in edits.ts. It returns {palette, movedStones, maxDeltaE} and is built from addPaletteColor and removePaletteColor. Do not build a full reorder remap, since that renumbers codes and makes printed sheets wrong.
2) Invariant guard. Add assertPaletteIndices(data, palette) to src/core/edits.ts (or types.ts). It scans c1/c2 (only where kind uses them), sub and free, and returns the maximum index. Call it:
   - in useProject's loader after unpackMosaic;
   - in the stats worker;
   - at the start of buildPdf and buildCsv.
   On a violation, do not print magenta stones or undercounted totals. Show a clear error ('Farbzuordnung beschädigt – bitte neu berechnen'), block PDF/CSV export and offer a recompute.
3) Tests in tests/core.test.ts:
   - Compute in custom mode from 12 materials, run the merge, and assert that every piece keeps its hex, total pieces are unchanged and all indices are < palette.length.
   - Run the merge with a shrunk material list and assert that the moved-stone count equals the stones of the removed colours and that the total is unchanged.
   - buildCsv and buildPdf throw on out-of-range indices.
   Reproduction of the current failure modes: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/value-correctness-ui-state-3/remap_check.ts.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
